#2660. LeBron Log No. 6: A Rocky night, a shooting lesson and a fight over ‘Bron'

LeBron Log No. 6: A Rocky night, a shooting lesson and a fight over 'Bron' originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

It was another eventful week for LeBron James.

That's why we started the LeBron Log in the first place.

The King spent his latest week taking his teammates to the movies, fighting over his name in federal court and producing his best three-point shooting performance as a Sixer days after recording a podcast about the craft.

This week also marks 20 years since James faced the Sixers alongside Allen Iverson.

James found an appropriate choice for the Sixers' latest team outing.

He organized a private screening of I Play Rocky on Friday night for players, their families and members of the basketball operations staff. The film follows Sylvester Stallone's fight to get the original Rocky made while insisting that he play the title character.

"I mean, it's Rocky. We in Philly," James said. "I heard it was a great movie, and we had a night off. I've got a few connections, and I was able to bring that to my teammates and this organization for us to watch it. I thought it was a great movie. Unbelievably cast. Everyone looked like exactly who they were portraying. That is Hollywood for you. It was pretty cool."

The Sixers shared photos of James alongside Jaylen Brown, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, Labaron Philon Jr., Jabari Walker, Tacko Fall and Adem Bona.

"Movie night, courtesy of LeBron," the team wrote.

The nationwide release of I Play Rocky came less than two weeks before Philadelphia celebrates the 50th anniversary of the original film on Dec. 3.

Nick Nurse could not attend because of a previous commitment, but he received positive reviews from his players.

"They went, they said it was very good, they loved it," Nurse said. "The big takeaway was how much Anthony actually looked like Rocky. Or Sylvester Stallone. One in the same."

James' first season in Philadelphia now includes a private Rocky screening. A trip up the Art Museum steps remains available for a future edition.

James and Steve Nash devoted the latest episode of their Mind the Game podcast to the art of shooting.

The two examined shooting form, confidence, repetitions, free throws and some of their favorite jumpers. James also revealed one detail that can affect what he does after catching the ball.

"I'm a guy who don't like shooting against the laces," James said. "So sometimes I'll come up on a quick stop and I'm about to raise and I can feel the laces not fixed. I'll turn that into a pump fake."

The episode was released Nov. 17, while James was experiencing an extended struggle from three-point range. It did not provide an instant fix.

James went 1 for 5 from three against Orlando and missed his lone attempt against Milwaukee. He entered Monday night's meeting with Portland shooting 21.7 percent from deep through his first 13 games.

James made all three of his first-half attempts from three. He ended the second quarter by pump-faking, stepping to his left and beating the buzzer with a corner three that tied the game at 69.

Nobody could see where the laces sat on the catch. The pump fake was clear.

James finished 4 for 5 from three and scored a season-high 23 points on 8-for-13 shooting. It was his third consecutive game with at least 20 points, following 22 against Orlando and 21 against Milwaukee.

The Sixers lost to Portland, 128-111, but James produced his best long-range performance since joining them.

Six days after discussing the art of shooting, he provided a brief demonstration.

James is also attempting to protect one of his most recognizable nicknames.

James and LBJ Trademarks LLC filed a federal lawsuit on Nov. 17 against PlayVision Inc. and its founders over a sports-betting research app initially called "Bron."

The complaint alleges that the company used an AI-generated version of James in an advertisement without his permission. The figure wore a No. 23 jersey with "Bron" across the back and resembled James through its voice, build and tattoos.

It also scrolled through wagers involving NBA players.

The lawsuit alleges that the advertisement falsely created the impression that James endorsed the app and suggested that he considered betting on NBA games. The complaint said the video received roughly 1 million views before it was removed.

"The integrity of NBA competition, and the public's confidence that players are not betting on the games they play, is of paramount importance to the league, its players and its fans," the complaint said. "Any suggestion that an active NBA player is betting on NBA games is therefore far from a trivial matter, and it should not be used for clicks and views."

The app offered odds comparisons, betting trends and tracking tools but did not directly accept wagers, according to its developer.

PlayVision renamed it "Evie" on Nov. 18, one day after James filed the lawsuit. James is seeking an injunction and unspecified damages. The case remains active in the Southern District of New York.

CLEVELAND – NOVEMBER 25: LeBron James #23 of the Cleveland Cavaliers looks to pass off when double teamed by the Philadelphia 76ers November 25, 2006 at The Quicken Loans Arena in Cleveland, Ohio. Copyright 2006 NBAE (Photo by David Liam Kyle/NBAE via Getty Images)

James spent Thanksgiving weekend in 2006 on the other side of the Sixers-Cavaliers matchup.

On Nov. 25, 2006, a 21-year-old James recorded 25 points, 11 assists, four rebounds and one block in Cleveland's 108-95 win over Philadelphia.

Donning the Cavs' old-school orange threads, he played nearly 41 minutes.

Iverson led the Sixers with 31 points. Andre Iguodala added 17 points and eight rebounds, while Kyle Korver made three three-pointers off the bench.

James recorded 11 assists that night. Nearly 20 years later, another 11-assist performance against Indiana moved him past Jason Kidd for third place in NBA history.

The 2006 meeting also came near the end of Iverson's original run with Philadelphia. The Sixers traded him to Denver less than a month later.

James was 21. Iverson was nearing his departure.

Twenty years later, James is wearing a Sixers uniform and Iverson's No. 3 hangs above his home floor.

#2656. Mike Tomlin on current Steelers situation: "It's a dumpster fire"

Many folks in and around football have had opinions about the recent brouhaha between former Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers and Steelers coach Mike McCarthy. Few have the insight and perspective that former Steelers coach Mike Tomlin brings to the table.

Appearing on NBC’s Chiefs-Bills halftime show on Thanksgiving night, Tomlin shared his thoughts on the situation in a conversation with Mike Tirico. (A portion of it was on the live broadcast; the full interview is here.)

“I had a range of emotions watching those course of events yesterday,” Tomlin told Tirico. “I think the prevailing one is just general sadness. Sad on a micro level, sad on a macro level. And by that, I mean, you know, just from an individual perspective, sad that we might be looking at the end of a legendary career of the quarterback, Aaron Rodgers, and just on the macro level, whether it’s organizationally or for the game of football at large, to see laundry aired out that way in a public forum.

“Those are things that kind of run counterculture to professional football. So, just a lot of emotions, but probably more than anything, man, general sadness on a lot of levels.”

Tirico asked Tomlin if he was shocked by Rodgers’s decision to air dirty laundry in a public forum.

“It certainly did,” Tomlin said, “but, you know, and particularly because I know both men involved, certainly had a lot of intimate work and development of relationship with Aaron over the last couple of years, and have known and competed against Mike, you know, respected and appreciated him as a coach for a long time. But I don’t — what I acknowledge is I don’t know them as a collective, the nature of their relationships, and so certainly I was surprised by that.”

Regardless of Rodgers’s conduct on the way out the door, Tomlin explained that Rodgers was viewed favorably by his teammates in 2025.

“He was beloved, and I’m not, you know, over-exaggerating that,” Tomlin said. “He worked at it, and people appreciated his openness to getting to know and understand the Steeler culture, to be engaged with teammates, and particularly from my perspective, I worked with a lot of veteran players over the years and at times they lose a little patience for the process, or they lose patience for relationships with younger guys, et cetera. Man, he seemed to embrace all of that and really embrace it in a real, natural way. He was a tireless worker regarding the process.

“I called early-morning quarterback meetings on Wednesday and Thursday. He was always early and engaged. Did a heck of a job in terms of engaging and developing, assisting in the development of young players. Specifically, Will Howard was always in that meeting, and, shoot, man, [Rodgers] and I were shoulder-to-shoulder in terms of the development of Will and challenging Will to develop professional habits. And so, you know, it was early and extremely consistent during my time with him, in terms of his willingness to work in those areas, and I think that’s why he’s so beloved in that locker room, as been reported by multiple sources in light of this incident. That is real. The guys in that locker room love and appreciate Aaron Rodgers.”

Had Tomlin gotten any sense that things were so close to breaking down?

“Absolutely none, but it’s a really specific reason why, to be honest with you, man,” Tomlin said. “One of my cultural mantras, when I worked there for the 19 years, is don’t talk to people about your problems unless they can be a component of the solution. Because if you do, it’s counterproductive, and people know where I stand there. And by that I mean if you have a problem with your playing time, don’t talk to your teammate about it. Talk to somebody that can do something about it. That’s problem solving.

“And so everybody understands my posture on some of that stuff, and so although I have really good, fluid communication with many of those guys, particularly, the more veteran guys, they know me and know me well enough to know that I didn’t want to hear about any potential issues, because I’m not a component of the solution. And so although, particularly, like, Cam Heyward, he and I spent a little time together doing his bye week. Man, we had no mention of anything bubbling under the surface, if you will.”

Can McCarthy effectively lead the team, given what Rodgers said?

“You know, it certainly created some challenges and challenges is probably an understatement if all of those things are true,” Tomlin told Tirico. “And certainly the ‘1-2-3 Packers’ is, because he acknowledged that. But his ability to overcome that or inability to overcome that in my opinion is based on relationships and the depth of those relationships and how those guys feel about him, or how those guys buy into what he’s selling. And so, certainly, he’s been there a short period of time. And so it makes you wonder, the level of that challenge. But it’ll be relationship-based, his ability to overcome the things that you mentioned.”

How does Tomlin think the Steelers will fare against the Broncos on Friday?

“Based on my knowledge of the men, particularly the leaders, the longstanding guys, they’ll do a great job of getting hyper-focused on what really matters, and that’s that football game,” Tomlin said. “They’ll use it as a mantra to bring them together. I expect those guys to fight. Now, fight and quality play are two different things. I’m certainly not gonna expect those guys not to fight. I think they’re gonna fight and fight extremely hard. What I’m interested in is quality of play, quality of execution. And those are things that could be impacted by the level of distraction that they had on a short week in particular.”

Tirico then asked Tomlin how he feels, overall, about what has transpired this week.

“I’m upset about it, you know, it’s a dumpster fire,” Tomlin said. “And I don’t say that in a judgmental way. I presided over a few dumpster fires in my 19 years. But it certainly is upsetting, and I’m sure Steeler Nation is upset.”

If owner Art Rooney II calls Tomlin for advice, what would Tomlin say?

“Hey, Mike, that’s a hypothetical, because I know he wouldn’t and, and because I know how he’s trained,” Tomlin said. “You know, Art is a guy that’s not a hedge fund guy that bought a football team. He’s not a, you know, artificial intelligence guy that bought a football team. This is a family business. It’s generational. Any advice or thought process in that way, I imagine he just says, ‘What would my dad do?’ Or, ‘What would my grandfather do?’ Their mode of operation is time tested, it’s generational. And so, I doubt, very, very seriously, that he called anyone for outside advice.”

Finally, Tirico asked whether Tomlin believes Rodgers will get another NFL opportunity this season, if he wants one.

“There’s certainly a possibility for that,” Tomlin said. “And I just say that based on the 19 years that I held the position that I held. It’s a 32-team league. All it takes is one. Over time, I’ve laughed and watched that people talk about, you know, ‘No, that could never happen.’ In a 32-team league, when everybody is highly competitive and there’s some real challenges, particularly as you get to this portion of the journey from a player availability standpoint, there’s certainly a possibility if he desires that he could play again, because all it takes is one suitor.”

Having cleared waivers, Rodgers is available to that one suitor, if/when that one suitor calls. Still, that one suitor will need to be willing to accept the risk that, if Rodgers doesn’t have things go the way he wants, he’ll choose to do again the same thing he did this week.

#2653. 4 instant takeaways from the Chiefs’ last-second loss in Buffalo

The Kansas City Chiefs fought to the end of a messy, low-scoring game against the Buffalo Bills, but ultimately fell 13-10. Here are four takeaways from Thanksgiving night:

From the jump, Kansas City's defense was ready for a long evening of containing James Cook and taking on the battering ram that is Josh Allen. On a rainy evening, Buffalo used a high-volume run game to control the contest, but the Chiefs never allowed Cook to gain more than 10 yards on any of his 32 carries.

Buffalo's running backs were held to 3.4 yards per carry, but quarterback Josh Allen gained 43 yards on the ground and found room for a 17-yard gash at one point. However, the Chiefs' coverage was tight and held Allen to just 81 yards and two interceptions on 10 of 21 passing; he finished with an 18.3 passer rating.

The Bills were able to march in the red zone a couple of times that Kansas City eventually forced to a screeching halt with clutch interceptions by cornerback Nohl Williams and safety Alohi Gilman.

As a low-scoring game came to a close, defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo dialed up the blitz to contain Allen in the pocket and bring him to the ground multiple times. From start to finish, the Chiefs' defense played winning football on Thanksgiving night…

… and the special teams unit did not play winning football. If you thought the conditions of the game were sloppy, the performance of the special teams topped it.

Whether it was a dropped kickoff, a dropped punt, a misfielded punt backed up deep, netting eight yards on a punt or the various penalties, it was a typical first half for the Chiefs' special teams unit. Unfortunately, the miscues kept coming, including a 46-yard field goal missed by the over-trusted Harrison Butker.

At the very end, punter Matt Araiza was backed up and had his punt tipped, setting up enough of a return for the Bills' game-winning field goal. It was a gross night for long-time special teams coordinator Dave Toub's unit.

From the opening drive, an apparent miscommunication between rookie left tackle Kahlil Benson and left guard Kingsley Suamataia left edge defender Bradley Chubb unblocked to make the third-and-one stop, it was a rough showing for the Chiefs' offensive line.

Backups Hunter Nourzad and Fred Johnson were inserted into the game and had costly penalties in the second half, but those were not the only two flags on the Chiefs' offensive line. One of the most crucial was called on left guard Kingsley Suamataia after the snap, which took Kansas City from a manageable third down to a third and long they were unable to convert.

Quarterback Patrick Mahomes and running back Emmett Johnson found space to make plays enough times to give the Chiefs a fighting chance, but the offense was overcoming backups up front as much as the rain in this one.

After the football world had its mind blown with Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington's non-catch a few weeks ago, wide receiver Rashee Rice's catch on the field being overturned was the latest in the storied history of "what is a catch?"

No one will seemingly ever have a confident answer to that question. Alas, it wasn't the reason Kansas City lost this game, just an insane call.

It’s unclear whether he was interacting with Cowboys fans or Eagles fans. He appeared to be making an aggressive movement toward someone before DiSandro intervened.

The Eagles contend that Sirianni was celebrating with Eagles fans, and that Sirianni was pulled away so that he could shake the hand of Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer after the game.

There was never any contact (at least none that the cameras captured). Still, it’s a bad look — and it’s definitely on brand.

While Sirianni has yet to cross the line, it seems like he will, one of these days.

Regardless, the Eagles have now won two in a row after losing seven in a row. They’re 4-7 and on the fringes of contention in the NFC East.

#2640. Could Chloe Kelly really miss out on England's Women's World Cup squad? Lionesses legend again facing selection battle despite big-game pedigree

The Arsenal winger was the hero at Euros of both 2022 and 2025, despite her participation in both tournaments being in doubt for a long time, and as the summer approaches, a similar story is unfolding

If anyone is experiencing a case of deja vu when it comes to Lionesses star Chloe Kelly right now, it's understandable. In seven months' time - granted they expectedly come through next week's play-off with Ukraine - England should be kicking-off their Women's World Cup campaign. However, as was the case two years ago as the 2025 European Championship loomed, and five years ago as Euro 2022 neared, the chances of Kelly, one of this team's biggest stars, being there appear are far from certain.

It's been a recurring theme in Kelly's career to date, which is especially strange given each of the three cases have been for entirely different reasons. At the end of 2021, Kelly was in the middle of a long recovery from a devastating ACL injury; at the end of 2024, she was dramatically out of favour at Manchester City, to the point that she wasn't even making some matchday squads; and right now, as 2026 nears its conclusion, a puzzling hamstring problem is keeping her on the sidelines, with her most recent minutes coming back in September.

For some, it might seem like an irrelevant topic: If Kelly is fit when the World Cup comes around, she will surely be in the squad, right? She has too much big-game pedigree to be left out by Sarina Wiegman, especially given squads have finally been expanded to incorporate 26 players.

But the longer Kelly's rather vague absence continues, the more that line of thinking is thrown into doubt. She was the match-winner in the Euro 2022 final and it was her penalty that decided the shootout in the showpiece event in 2025. But could the Lionesses' icon really find herself watching the 2027 Women's World Cup from home?

Kelly has accumulated so many big moments in her England career to date, with her winner in the Euro 2022 final the most notable

The catalogue of big moments that Kelly has built up in an England shirt over the last few years is quite remarkable.

To score an extra-time winner against Germany, at Wembley, in the Euro 2022 final to deliver the Lionesses' first-ever major tournament triumph, and on home soil, guaranteed that Kelly would be an England icon no matter what else happened in her career, even if she was only 24 years old at the time.But to follow that up with numerous moments of magic at the subsequent Euros has added massively to her legend.

It wasn't just one big moment like in 2022, but rather several spread out across one of the most dramatic knockout-stage runs in the history of the game. Her decisive spot-kick in the penalty shootout win over Spain in the final was the headline contribution, but she also scored the extra-time winner in the semi-final against Italy and provided the cross that kickstarted the incredible comeback in the quarters, before scoring in the shootout as Sweden's hearts were broken.

There have been other highlights too, such as the thunderous penalty - so powerful it generated headlines aplenty for its speed - that won the last-16 shootout against Nigeria at the 2023 Women's World Cup, as part of England's run to the final.

Regardless of questions about form and a lack of game time, some would argue that Kelly should be on the plane to the World Cup whatever the case, granted she is fit

It all contributes to the reputation Kelly has carved out as a serious big-game player - and it's not as if she is limited to these moments either. After joining Man City in 2020, Kelly would spend the majority of the next five years marking herself out as one of the best wingers in the Women's Super League, before it ended on a strangely sour note.

When she found a way out from her exile via a loan to Arsenal, she reminded everyone of those qualities with a tremendous second half of the 2024-25 season, which served as an excellent response to being left out of an England squad for the first time under Wiegman. Her contributions in the Champions League were particularly notable, helping the Gunners to defy the odds and win the trophy. It paved the way for a return to the Lionesses squad ahead of Euro 2025, where she took centre stage as England retained their title.

Match-winning qualities, penalty-taking expertise and an ability to rise to the biggest of occasions - regardless of form, Kelly will surely be in Wiegman's 2027 Women's World Cup squad... right?!

It feels difficult at this moment to guarantee Kelly's fitness, and there are concerns about her form too, which wasn't at a high level before her ongoing absence began

But none of this is even a conversation if Kelly isn't fit. Her last game came on September 27, when she played 30 minutes from the bench in Arsenal's 1-0 defeat to Chelsea. Two days later, she wasn't in the England squad. Explaining her absence, Wiegman said that Kelly's "levels" on the pitch "weren't what I expected". When asked if there was any injury that contributed to her decision, the England boss replied: "For me, it's just what I saw on the pitch."

Bizarrely, when Arsenal boss Renee Slegers faced the media just a few hours later, she revealed Kelly was unavailable for the next day's Champions League clash with Paris FC. "She's had some issues with her hamstring," she explained. "Nothing we could see from an injury perspective. [She's] been managing something and at the moment not available to play."

Later in the press conference, Slegers confirmed that Kelly had indeed been available for selection for England too: "She played on Sunday. She played 30-plus minutes for us, so at that point she was fit and available."

Such vagueness has endured when Slegers has been asked about Kelly in the two months since. Last week, ahead of Sunday's draw with West Ham, she said the forward was "still managing the same hamstring issues", adding: "There's no timeline [for her return] at the moment."

Will Kelly complete another redemption story ahead of the World Cup - or will this ending come with disappointment rather than glory?

It's all set up for another of Kelly's trademark redemption stories. In 2022, she bounced back from the devastating ACL injury which ruled her out of the Olympic Games in 2021 and the majority of the following season, returning just in time to make the Euro 2022 squad. Once there, she made her mark with the title-winning goal.

In 2024, she endured what she'd later describe as a "dark time" at Man City, where she was completely out of favour and dropped from the England squad due to a lack of game time, with just four months to go until Euro 2025. A loan to Arsenal was secured at the 11th hour in the January transfer window and her road to redemption began, culminating in her becoming a European champion with club and country, providing decisive moments in both triumphs.

Will the difficulties of 2026 have a similar ending? When the 2027 Women's World Cup concludes in July, will we be talking about how Kelly overcame these frustrating fitness issues, and a lack of form before them, to make Wiegman's squad and deliver a moment that helped the Lionesses win the tournament for the first time? Or will it be different this time around? Right now, Kelly is running out of time to book her ticket on the plane to Brazil?

#2639. Tyler Bass hits walk-off 57-yard field goal, Bills beat Chiefs 13-10

The weather in Western New York delivered nasty conditions with freezing rain for Thanksgiving night.

Buffalo’s kicker sent a walk-off, 57-yard field goal through the uprights to give the Bills a 13-10 victory over the Chiefs, putting the club further in the driver’s seat for the AFC’s No. 1 seed.

The game was not without controversy, particularly late in the contest. But the weather conditions also affected both teams, as neither offense got much going.

Josh Allen finished the game 10-of-21 for 81 yards with two interceptions, rushing for 43 yards on seven attempts. Allen’s passer rating of 18.3 is the second lowest of his career in any regular-season game.

Patrick Mahomes completed 16-of-29 passes for 174 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions.

James Cook ended up pacing the offense for Buffalo, rushing for 117 yards on 32 carries with Buffalo’s only touchdown — a 5-yard run in the second quarter.

The Chiefs got a 26-yard field goal from Harrison Butker to close the first half and a 1-yard touchdown from Emmett Johnson to open the second half. But the team was not able to score again.

After Bass connected on a 54-yard field goal in the fourth quarter to tie the game at 10-10, Butker missed his eighth field goal of the year — this one going wide right from 46 yards out.

Kansas City had the ball with another shot to get Butker in field goal range. But what looked like a third-down completion from Mahomes to Rahsee Rice was overturned on replay, allowing Buffalo to field another punt.

The Chiefs got yet another opportunity to possess the ball after Allen was sacked for the second time on the night. But the club’s special teams continued to have issues, with Josh Downs fielding a punt inside the 10, returning it to just the 11-yard line.

And when Mahomes’ third-down pass to an open Kelce fell incomplete, Matt Ariza’s punt was short and skipped to Greg Dortch, who returned 17 yards to the Kansas City 39 with four seconds on the clock.

Somehow in the weather conditions, that was enough for Bass, who sent the 57-yard attempt through the uprights to give the Bills their 10th win of the season.

Between Butker, Downs’ returns, and Ariza’s punts, the Chiefs special teams had a rough night, arguably costing the team the game.

On the injury front, Chiefs receiver/returner Jalen Royals (ankle) exited and was not able to return.

With the win, the Bills are now 10-1 and will have at least a one-game lead on the rest of the conference entering Week 13 for the No. 1 seed. Buffalo will play division-rival New England in Week 13.

The Chiefs are now 8-3 and won’t have extra rest in the coming week, as they’ll be in Los Angeles to face the Rams next Thursday night.

#2636. James can still take over ‘any given moment,' and Sixers trust he'll pick right spots

James can still take over 'any given moment,' and Sixers trust he'll pick right spots originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

LeBron James isn't oblivious to the calendar and the clock.

He knows he'll turn 42 years old next month, he's ancient by NBA standards and decline is inevitable.

James also knows who he is and what he still can do, whatever the norms are for players of a certain age.

"I think his battle against Father Time is one of the most impressive things he's done over the course of his entire career," Heat head coach Erik Spoelstra said Wednesday before Miami's loss to the Sixers. "We all know and everybody always says that Father Time always wins. But right now he's giving Father Time hell."

James went on to record his first triple-double with the 15-4 Sixers, posting 25 points, 12 assists and 10 rebounds. The four-time MVP is at 126 regular-season triple-doubles and counting in his career.

Only Russell Westbrook, Nikola Jokic, Oscar Robertson and Magic Johnson have more in NBA history. James is 17 above Philadelphia native and Sixers legend Wilt Chamberlain.

With Joel Embiid sidelined by illness for a second consecutive game and Jaylen Brown ruled out at halftime with left hamstring tightness, James' do-it-all performance was timely. Tyrese Maxey's 30-point, six-assist outing was essential, too.

"I'm just trying to play the game the right way," James said. "I don't think my job is to dominate the game every night for this ball club. We have a Finals MVP (Brown), we have a regular-season MVP (Embiid), we have an up-and-coming superstar at point guard, we've got a young fella in VJ (Edgecombe) who's up and coming as well.

"My dues are paid with what I've done. If they need me to dust off the cape from time to time, then I can still accomplish that. But that's not my job. … But if they need it, I can do it at any given moment."

James' night featured a flurry of very deep three-pointers in the second quarter.

He started the season 10 for 46 beyond the arc (21.7 percent), but his percentage has risen to 31.6 with two sweet-shooting games in a row.

"The work has been put in and I'm not ever worried about anything as far as my game," he said. "The difference between the start of the season and now is that my legs are feeling better, my ramp-up is feeling better.

"I'm about to be 42 years old in a month. S—, it takes a little bit longer for the ramp-up, but I've been feeling pretty good as of late. I don't ever second-guess myself … because I know the work that I put in."

While James' rebounding was perhaps the least spectacular aspect of his game, Sixers head coach Nick Nurse appreciated his work on the boards.

James has remained a statistically solid defensive rebounder into his 40s and he's one reason why the Sixers have made a major improvement in that department. According to Cleaning the Glass, the Sixers' opponents have grabbed 28.4 percent of their own misses, which ranks sixth in the NBA. The team ranked 27th last season.

Asked about James' cape comments, Maxey shouted out, "Dust it off then!" with a grin.

Maxey's not sure exactly when James will dramatically elevate his game, but he trusts the 22-time All-Star to pick the right spots.

"I don't know," Maxey said. "Early in the game, he was telling me he was tired. I said, 'Well, we don't have time for you to be tired.'

"But he does a good job of just managing the game. He knows when he needs to score, he knows when he needs to pass. We're going to need a lot from him. I know he's seasoned, but we expect a lot of him and he does that."

#2635. Kimmi Ascanio: The USWNT prospect dubbed 'mini Tobin Heath' but showing Keira Walsh-like traits

The San Diego Wave teenager started life as a promising forward but she's since transitioned into a holding midfielder, and has already caught the eye of U.S. boss Emma Hayes

When Kimmi Ascanio, the San Diego Wave's talented 18-year-old, was a guest on the RE-CAP Show in February, a podcast hosted by United States women's national team legends Tobin Heath and Christen Press, it was always going to be a must-watch. Ascanio has been likened to Heath throughout the early stages of what looks to be a promising career, so to see her actually meet and converse at length with the iconic winger was sure to be interesting.

Funnily enough, in the time since the show came out, Ascanio has actually adopted a position in the Wave line-up that is essentially foreign to Heath. Long an exciting forward like Heath, Ascanio transformed into an integral holding midfielder in the 2026 season - one so important, even, that her absence from the play-offs due to injury was a "serious issue", in the opinion of three-time NWSL champion McCall Zerboni, as the Wave crashed out. "She's more important than people realize," Zerboni added on CBS Sports Golazo.

But Heath's view on the similarities she shares with this teenage phenom were never rooted in a position on the field. "It's more so how she moves with and without the ball," she explained. "I definitely see the comparisons." Press agreed. "You move through space similarly," she observed. However, Press' main takeaway from sharing a conversation with the pair was rooted in their personalities. "I had a 'Freaky Friday' moment," she proclaimed. "I saw Tobin 20 years ago sitting next to Tobin today."

At one point, when Ascanio explained how she likes to meet with the coaching staff to analyse her game, and sheepishly declared that she doesn't like meeting with the head coach but rather those around him, Press interjected with astonishment: "Oh my gosh, you just are like Tobin!"

Understandably, while still just 18, Ascanio is a little shy at points as she chatted to two icons of U.S. women's soccer, one of whom she is obviously flattered to be compared to. "If there's one person I'd want to be compared to, it would be Tobin," she rather heart-warmingly shared.

But none of that is related to a lack of confidence. Ascanio is not just one of the most talented young players coming through in the NWSL and the U.S. youth national teams; as her recent nomination to the NWSL's Second XI for the 2026 season and her inclusion on the USWNT's CONCACAF W Championship preliminary roster shows, she is also a player making her mark at the top level right now.

Though a more dedicated tennis player in her youth, it didn't take long for Ascanio to mark herself as a top soccer prospect once she changed her focus

Incredibly, Ascanio didn't even start playing soccer in an organised format until she was around 10 or 11 years old. Born in Orlando, Florida, to Venezuelan parents from a Spanish background, the sport was a feature in her life before then, with her family always having it on the television and her brother also playing it. "I love Real Madrid and my brother loves Barcelona," she explained.

But it was tennis that Ascanio got into first. While she would play soccer casually with her brother, it was only when she was watching him play one day and his coach needed an extra participant that everything changed. "From then on, I let go of tennis," she said.

Alongside the youth club soccer she played with Florida United, heavy exposure to futsal would help to accelerate Ascanio's potential in a sport she picked up in a more dedicated sense quite late, something which is evident in her outstanding technique. Soon enough, the talented teenager was a mainstay in the U.S. youth national teams, helping her country win continental titles at Under-15 and Under-17 level.

Her contributions at the U17 CONCACAF Women's Championship were particularly notable: As the youngest player in the squad, Ascanio scored a six-minute hat-trick in the semi-final win over Haiti and also netted in the final, a 4-0 victory over Mexico. Later that year, Ascanio also stood out at the U17 World Cup, starting every game in the U.S's best performance at the tournament for 16 years, as the team finished third.

Ascanio signed her first contract with the San Diego Wave when she was just 16 years old and became an important starter the following season

It was just a few weeks after that tournament that Ascanio was catapulted into the limelight, signing a three-year contract with the San Diego Wave just two months after she had celebrated her 16th birthday. The versatile teenager had spent some time with the club in pre-season and they did not hesitate to secure her signature after witnessing up close what she was capable of.

"We saw Kimmi's ability to transition to the professional game and we were thoroughly impressed," Molly Downtain, then the Wave's general manager, noted.

Unsurprisingly, Ascanio's game time didn't come immediately, with her making just six appearances in 2024. But those opportunities increased the following season, with her able to evolve into a consistent starter relatively quickly, setting her up for a big 2026.

Ascanio continued to be a key player for San Diego in the 2026 season, albeit in a brand new role

How Ascanio performed in the 2026 season was tremendous. Only eight players in the NWSL played more accurate passes in the final third than her, only one of whom was a San Diego team-mate. Among the Wave's squad, Ascanio ranked fifth for key passes, fourth for accurate passes and also provided three assists, despite transitioning from a forward role to that of a defensive midfielder during the season.

In that new role, she was able to provide a steady presence in front of the San Diego back line, ranking third in the squad for tackles and fifth for interceptions, while also linking defence and attack in possession. Somehow, she became one of the best in the position in the NWSL almost overnight, as well as one of San Diego's most important players.

Her absence in the post-season hurt the Wave, who lost to the Utah Royals in the quarter-finals. "Losing Ascanio did change their dynamic quite a bit," Zerboni noted after the game.

A place in the NWSL's Second XI on awards night was a consolation, though her absence from the list of nominees for Midfielder of the Year was a surprise, while her presence on the USWNT's preliminary roster for the CONCACAF W Championship showed that she is on Emma Hayes' radar too.

Boasting great technical skill and awareness, Ascanio's seamless transition into a new position has highlighted a lot of her strengths

Ascanio's outstanding technical skill is the first thing that stands out when watching her play. She's simply brilliant with the ball at her feet, something explained wonderfully by Heath on the RE-CAP Show: "I like her relationship with football. I think that's what I always look at when I'm looking at top talent. Are they friends with the ball? It's so clear to me the players that have a relationship with the football and Kimmi absolutely is in love with that thing."

Being so good on the ball no doubt plays a role in how calm Ascanio is when she comes under pressure. That's all the more important now that she has dropped back into a deeper midfield role, where not losing possession is more of a priority when compared to the attacking positions she has occupied in the past.

Aiding Ascanio's strong transition into this new role has been her great awareness, how consistently she keeps her head up and checks her surroundings, and also her strong positional discipline, which is especially impressive given her situation. While still only boasting a slight physique at this stage, she is dogged and scrappy when it comes to putting opponents under pressure, and her work rate out of possession is impactful.

The teenager can still provide an attacking threat from deep too, with a smart pass forward often followed up by a charge up the field to add another number into the final third, while her vision and passing range also still helps carve out opportunities for team-mates.

Still just 18 years old, Ascanio has plenty of room for growth, despite already being an impactful player in a top league

There are still things for Ascanio to get used to in the senior game and also in her new position. She can still sometimes play a slightly riskier or trickier pass to control while in that deeper role, probably because she is still getting used to that smaller margin for error in defensive areas, which can lead to turnovers.

She can - and likely will - grow to demand the ball from her team-mates more often too, especially from the defence and her goalkeeper. After all, she has the ability to dictate games and she should lean into that.

There will also be a natural increase in strength as she spends more time in the senior game and matures as a player in this environment. That said, she does plenty of good work in her defensive actions even with that to come.

Though regularly compared to Heath, Ascanio's move to a holding midfield role has highlighted similarities she shares with England's Walsh

Holding midfielders come in all different shapes and sizes. There are physical, disruptive ones; there are diminutive, scrappy ones; there are players whose strengths are more in out of possession work and winning the ball back for others to then do damage with; there are others whose deeper role is centred around the dictating and controlling of play, rather than being an enforcer.

At this stage, Ascanio appears to align more with a holding midfielder like Keira Walsh. The teenager is the first to admit that she is not particularly strong or fast, things which have made her lean into her technical skill more throughout her development. It means she is instead the sort of midfielder who dictates games and controls them from deep with her great passing range, vision and calmness on the ball.

Like Walsh, she can still be effective in thwarting the opponent, able to cover space well and read the game to intercept passes or recover the ball. But rather than being an all-action holding midfielder with stand-out defensive strengths - like, say, a Lena Oberdorf - the emphasis is more on Ascanio's distribution, while still asking her to snuff out danger as it appears in front of the back line.

Of course, there is also a world in which Ascanio reverts back to a more attacking role and showcases more of the traits that earned her comparisons to Heath. For now, though, she is excelling in midfield.

After a huge 2026, it'll be fascinating to see what 2027 has in store for Ascanio - especially with a senior World Cup on the horizon

It'll be fascinating to see how Ascanio builds on this 2026 season, not least because it looks like she could be about to leave not only the San Diego Wave in this off-season, but the NWSL as a whole. The teenager's contract expires in the coming months, and The Cutback has reported that she is set to leave when it does, amid interest from clubs in the U.S. and Europe. Soccerdonna, meanwhile, believes London City Lionesses are the front-runners for her signature.

It would be an interesting move for several reasons. It'd expose Ascanio to a new league with different styles of play, plus all the off-field baggage that comes with moving abroad for the first time, which could be a valuable experience to further mature this impressive 18-year-old. Joining London City would also put her in a midfield with none other than Alexia Putellas, who won her third Ballon d'Or just last month.

Some have raised concerns that Ascanio might not get the same level of game time at London City, but while the club does have a number of options in that holding midfield role, it is Daniela Arques who has shrugged off most competition for the place, playing 830 of the team's 990 league minutes this term. Ascanio would be a sterner challenger for Arques' spot, which would be good news for a London City side pushing for Champions League football, if not the Women's Super League title.

Minutes will be important if Ascanio wants to push for that first full USWNT call-up. Her place on Hayes' CONCACAF W Championship preliminary roster earlier this month shows that it clearly isn't too far away, though it may not come in time for her to force her way into the picture for the 2027 Women's World Cup. Hayes has some great midfield options to pick from, after all.

However, a lot can change in six months. Wherever she is playing her football in the New Year, if Ascanio starts 2027 like she ended 2026, before that injury frustratingly ruled her out of the NWSL play-offs, then she will surely be rewarded by Hayes - and she will have earned the opportunity.

#2633. Andy Reid gives 2 injury updates after loss to Bills

#2631. MLB rumors: Mets to meet with NPB star, plus latest on Ketel Marte, Cubs, Mariners, Nationals, more

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

We're one week away from Thanksgiving and the offseason has started to pick up a little bit in Major League Baseball. We've seen an All-Star pitcher sign (Sonny Gray to the Twins) and a trade involving an All-Star (Maikel Garcia to the Mariners). The White Sox also signed a mid-rotation starter while the Red Sox grabbed a first baseman fresh off a World Series title. Is there enough time for a flurry of moves before the owners lock the players out when the CBA expires on Dec. 1?

In theory, there sure is. We can hold out hope, as there has been enough movement to keep belief alive.

It's no secret that the Diamondbacks are willing to trade All-Star second baseman Ketel Marte. A big hurdle might be his 10-and-5 no-trade rights and questions about which teams Marte would approve in a potential deal. Further, the asking price on Arizona's end is "very high," reports FanSided. Still, plenty of teams are said to be interested.

Marte, 33, has five years and $91.75 million left on his deal. He finished third in MVP voting in 2024, was a highly productive All-Star in 2025, but some issues arose in 2026, including several no-shows. He hit .249/.316/.432 (107 OPS+) with 2.5 WAR and some possible clubhouse baggage.

The Mets are planning a Zoom meeting with Japanese right-hander Kaima Taira, reports the New York Post. This won't have an impact on their pursuit of Tarik Skubal, just in case anyone is curious.

Taira, 27, has been one of the top pitchers in Japan's NPB for years. Last season, in 23 starts, he had a 1.36 ERA and 0.96 WHIP with 141 strikeouts in 146 innings. He's had a sub-2.00 ERA four of the last five seasons, with the exception being a 2.40 in 2023.

CBS Sports ranked Taira as the No. 19 free agent available this winter:

Listed at 5-foot-8, Taira gets outlier extension down the mound (close to seven feet despite his height), which creates a low release window. Hitters rarely see the ball come from where Taira releases it. He's not a gimmick pitcher either. Taira sits mid-90s with his four-seam fastball and backs it up with a cutter, sinker, sweeper, slider, changeup, and splitter. The sweeper and slider are distinct pitches, as are the changeup and splitter. The Seibu Lions used Taira as a reliever in 2024 and 2025, then started him in 2026, and he handled the assignment well. The breaking balls are just OK, and the fact of the matter is that pitchers this height don't often hold up under a starter's workload. I would assume the team that signs Taira will give him a chance to start. In the long run, though, he might be a reliever, perhaps even a multi-inning setup man. Seibu announced on Oct. 30 that Taira will be posted this offseason.

Because of the expected lockout, international free agents are working under an artificial Dec. 1 deadline to sign, rather than the normal posting window.

For now, the Mets' rotation starts with Nolan McLean and Christian Scott.

The Cubs' main focus is on pitching, as well it should be after having one of the worst pitching staffs in baseball along with one of the best collections of position-player talent. Still, both corner outfielders (Ian Happ and Seiya Suzuki) have hit free agency along with catcher Carson Kelly, so they can't just ignore the offense. On that front, the ballclub has "extensively scouted" Teruaki Sato, according to The Athletic.

Sato has played mostly third base, where the Cubs have Alex Bregman, but also has outfield experience and could simply serve as DH. In 143 games last season in NPB, Sato hit .306/.383/.609 with 40 doubles, 39 home runs and 106 RBI. His strikeout numbers are high, but sometimes that's the price to be paid for top-level power.

CBS Sports ranked Sato as the No. 4 free agent this winter:

He will play the entire 2027 season at age 28 and is coming off a .306/.383/.609 slash line with 39 home runs, which won him Japan's first Triple Crown since Munetaka Murakami in 2022. Sato has a similar skill set but is not quite Murakami 2.0. He doesn't have quite as much power (but has plenty of it) and won't walk nearly as often, but he does swing and miss a bunch and is unlikely to remain at the hot corner long-term. Sato is a very aggressive hitter who ran a 66% contact rate this past season. That is below the 77% MLB average. The consensus seems to be that he will land at first base or in a corner outfield spot if not next year, then soon. Murakami successfully overcame his contact issues to slug 35 homers in only 127 games around a hamstring injury. At minimum, that will have MLB teams reconsidering how they evaluate the Japan-to-MLB transition. Like Murakami, Sato carries risk, and like Murakami, his power makes that risk worth the dice roll.

After being one of the most disappointing teams in 2026 and having an active general manager, of course the Mariners weren't going to just sit around after one move. Sure enough, Jerry Dipoto told reporters on Wednesday that they are still looking to add a right-handed bat (remember, Randy Arozarena is a free agent) along with a veteran infielder and a left-handed reliever even after acquiring Garcia. And perhaps most importantly, Dipoto insisted that they do have the payroll flexibility to add all of this.

Further, he also said the rotation is set and no other starting pitchers will be moved. So it'll be Logan Gilbert, George Kirby, Bryan Woo, Emerson Hancock and Kade Anderson heading into next season.

Fresh off signing right-handed starter Dustin May, the White Sox are looking to add another starting pitcher "of similar magnitude," reports the Chicago Sun-Times.

Though the White Sox were one of baseball's best stories last season and made the playoffs, the rotation was very thin. Right now, they have Sean Burke, May, Taylor, Davis Martin and Anthony Kay as their top five and are looking to add another of May's ilk. Things are already looking much better.

The Nationals finished third in the majors in runs scored last season, believe it or not. They trailed only the Cubs and Brewers, scoring more than the Dodgers. The problem was that the pitching staff was mostly a mess. As such, it's no surprise they are after starters and The Athletic names three targets: lefty Kris Bubic, righty Brady Singer and Japanese import Kona Takahashi.

Bubic, 29, has battled shoulder and elbow injuries the past two seasons, but the upside was flashed in the first part of 2025. He made the All-Star team and had a 2.55 ERA through 20 starts and 116 ⅓ innings.

The 30-year-old Singer was 6-15 with a 5.85 ERA for the Reds last season in a disaster of a contract year, but he was productive in the previous two seasons.

Takahashi, 29, was 9-7 with a 2.64 ERA, 1.10 WHIP and 118 strikeouts in 143 ⅓ innings in NPB last season.

#2630. Observations after James posts triple-double, Sixers beat Heat in NBA Cup

Observations after James posts triple-double, Sixers beat Heat in NBA Cup originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

LeBron James posted his first triple-double as a Sixer on Wednesday night and led his team to a 111-104 win over the Heat at Xfinity Mobile Arena.

James notched his 126th career regular-season triple-double with 25 points, 12 assists and 10 rebounds for the 15-4 Sixers.

Tyrese Maxey scored 30 points and dished out six assists.

Giannis Antetokounmpo recorded 32 points and 14 rebounds for the 10-7 Heat.

The Sixers improved to 2-1 and Miami fell to 2-1 in Eastern Conference Group B of the NBA Cup.

Jaylen Brown was ruled out at halftime with left hamstring tightness. He had six points on 2-for-8 shooting over 17 minutes.

"He'll get some imaging and we'll get the update tomorrow," Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said.

Joel Embiid (illness) missed his second game in a row. The Sixers are set to visit the Pacers on Friday night in their final Cup group game.

"He's ill," Nurse said of Embiid. "I do not know whether he's going to Indiana yet or not. I guess we'll find that out late tomorrow afternoon."

Here are observations on the Sixers' victory over the Heat:

Nurse emphasized pregame that the Sixers needed an improved defensive performance.

"We've got to compete much better at the defensive end than we did Monday (against the Trail Blazers)," he said. "It's as simple as that."

The night did not begin in especially promising fashion on that front. Antetokounmpo powered through Brown and scored inside for the game's first bucket. His transition layup put Miami up 6-0. The Heat scored nine fast-break points in the first six minutes.

As he had Monday in the Sixers' loss to Portland, Jabari Walker started at center. He was among the Sixers who shared the daunting defensive assignment of Antetokounmpo.

Walker took a charge on the 10-time All-Star in the first quarter, but Antetounkmpo had a stellar start. He forcefully orchestrated Miami's offense, often plowing through the middle of the floor and finding efficient answers.

The Sixers' defense was better late in the first quarter and it didn't hurt when Antetokounmpo took a seat.

Maxey had an aggressive, productive first period, scoring 13 points. Dominick Barlow's tip-in gave the Sixers a 27-26 edge.

James drained three three-pointers early in the second quarter, including a confident, deep jumper that fired up a high-volume home crowd. He's shown that he remains capable of flipping a world-class switch and taking over games in a vast array of ways.

There's no question the 22-time All-Star is out of his early-season outside shooting slump. James has gone 8 for 11 from long range over his last two games. He's scored at least 20 points in four straight.

"I just play the game as it unfolds," James said. "I had a couple of opportunities and I was able to connect on them. I kind of know when my hand is feeling pretty good, especially from the outside. We'll see how long I can keep it going."

Adem Bona checked in early in the second quarter. He provided a string of excellent defensive possessions against Antetokounmpo, including an emphatic block and several well-guarded missed jumpers, although Bona did get called for three fouls in the second period.

Nurse was pleased with what he received defensively from both Bona (two blocks, six rebounds) and Barlow (nine points, eight rebounds) off the bench.

"They used their gifts," he said. "They're quick side to side, both of them. When they're in that kind of fighting mode like that … they did a good job. We tried to get Bona in there when Giannis was in, just for the rim protection. And Dom just played really, really (well) all over the place … on the defense, on the rebounding, on the running, on the cutting."

The Sixers played effective zone defense at the tail end of the second quarter and held a nine-point halftime lead. That grew as high as 16 points in the third quarter.

Miami pulled back within single digits, but the Sixers maintained a healthy advantage and James kept on making highlight plays. He lobbed the ball up to Edgecombe early in the fourth quarter and the second-year guard skied high to lay it in. James later connected with Barlow on an alley-oop.

Once the Sixers have a substantial lead, James' presence is a massive help offensively. He's very well-accustomed to conducting methodical half-court offense, identifying favorable matchups and turning to fruitful actions over and over. James will also still steam forward on the fast break when he sees the chance.

Maxey buried a step-back three to extend his team's lead to 111-95 with 2:29 on the clock and the Sixers polished off a professional win. The fans roared when James snatched the rebound required to reach his triple-double.

"We came out tonight with a different mentality, different energy," Maxey said. "Nurse got on us a little bit in the film (session) yesterday. He lit a fire for a lot of us, which is good. We needed it."

#2629. Luis Castillo trade grades: White Sox give up steady back-end starter to offload salary; Rockies get creative

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Two days after adding Dustin May to their rotation, the Chicago White Sox have subtracted Luis Castillo and Davis Martin. The White Sox are sending Castillo and Martin to the Colorado Rockies for lefty Sean Sullivan and minor-league catcher Douglas Veliz, the teams announced late Thursday. The Rockies will take on Castillo's entire contract.

Castillo, 33, joined the White Sox in a deadline trade with the Seattle Mariners. He struggled badly after the deal, allowing 30 runs in 31 innings, and he finished the season on the injured list with a shoulder issue. Castillo has one year remaining on his contract at $22.75 million, though a $25 million option for 2028 will vest if he throws 150 innings in 2027.

The 29-year-old Martin threw 146 innings with a 3.95 ERA in 2026, but it was a 3.41 ERA in the first half and a 5.12 ERA in the second half. The White Sox kept him at arm's length in the postseason despite running bullpen games almost nightly. Martin allowed two runs in one inning in his only postseason appearance.

Neither Sullivan nor Veliz are significant prospects. For all intents and purposes, the White Sox are attaching Martin to Castillo as a sweetener to get the Rockies to take Castillo's salary. The Rockies are essentially buying Martin, who is under team control through 2030, by taking on the rest of Castillo's contract.

Here now are our trade grades for this two-for-two swap.

Fair or not, I'm going to lump the two Castillo trades together. Chicago stepped out to acquire Castillo at the deadline and absorbed the $30 million or so remaining on his contract to do it. Seranthony Domínguez, who had about $15 million left on his deal, went the other way in the trade, so the White Sox took on about $15 million total, and also gave up a pretty good prospect in Boston Smith.

Four and a half months later, the White Sox had to give up a steady back-end starter in Martin to clear Castillo's money. They ended up saving about $7 million in 2027 in this series of moves, but it cost them Martin and Smith (and Domínguez), and they had to endure 31 awful innings from Castillo. Unless Sullivan or Veliz hit big, the White Sox took a series of Ls here.

Credit to president of baseball operations Chris Getz for acknowledging a mistake with Castillo and acting quickly to unload him. It was costly, though. Martin isn't a star, but cheap back-end starters are very valuable. We'll see what Getz & Co. do with the savings. Presumably they'll invest in more pitching. Having to give up Martin to dump Castillo so soon is a stinker, though. Ouch.

The Rockies need all types of pitching (righty, lefty, starter, reliever, whatever) and it's not often they can convince quality (or even competent) free agents to come to Coors Field. They have to develop their own pitchers or trade for pitching, and in this instance, they took on Castillo's hefty salary to get Martin and his four years of control. Creative, if nothing else.

There is downside potential too. Martin has run below league-average strikeout rates and middling ground ball rates throughout his career. Pitchers who allow a lot of balls in play -- a lot of balls in play in the air -- are a poor match for Coors Field. It's good the Rockies spent and found a way to add controllable pitching. They just might not have picked the best pitcher.

After losing 104 games in 2026, there is no such thing as a bad dart throw for the Rockies. It's unlikely they would have been able to spend the $22.75 million on a free agent (at least not without overpaying), so taking on Castillo to get Martin is the next best thing. I like the thinking, even if I don't love Martin's profile in Coors Field.

#2627. Important Jusuf Nurkic Injury Update

The Utah Jazz have had a dissapointing start to the season, but it looks like things might be changing for the better. According to the Utah Jazz, Jusuf Nurkic has been upgraded to questionable.

This is great news for the Utah Jazz because different elements of Nurkic's game should make life easier for the young core. Nurkic is a great screener, and the Jazz desperately need one. This season, the Jazz have the 6th-worst PPP (points per possession) at 0.84 when scoring off screens. They also have the 7th worst field goal percentage off screens at 35.9%. It's also worth noting that the Jazz are running the 8th-most off-screen trackable plays per game. That means the Jazz are running a lot of a play that hasn't worked well. Insert Nurkic and you should see this get better.

It doesn't stop there. Utah runs the fourth most dribble handoffs in the league while scoring the fourth-least PPP (Points Per Possession).

What does this mean? The Jazz are highly reliant on screens and dribble handoffs, and it has not gone well. Jusuf Nurkic is an ELITE screener. In 2025-26, can you guess who was the #1 player in the league in screen assists per game? You guessed it, Jusuf Nurkic.

We'll see if Nurkic comes back healthy and if he's moving well, but if he is, it's no understatement to say that this could turn the season around for Utah, considering the style of offense they run.

Now, it's just questionable and not probable, but for Utah to change the status is a good sign he will play.

#2626. Eagles coach Nick Sirianni pulled back from fans after Thanksgiving win over Cowboys, team claims he was celebrating

Emotions were high following the Philadelphia Eagles' comeback win over the Dallas Cowboys on Thanksgiving. Especially for Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni.

The immediate aftermath of the game saw Sirianni approach a group of field-level Eagles fans and exchange some high-fives, before looking at another group and getting pulled back by a pair of staffers. It's unclear what happened, but Sirianni appeared to maintain eye contact with someone and tried to force his way back before getting pulled to the field.

It was only a few seconds, but it drew attention on social media.

The simple explanation appeared to be Sirianni, who wears his heart on his sleeve in the best of times, was trying to get into it with the opposing fan base. The team and coach are claiming that wasn't the case.

While speaking with reporters postgame, Sirianni said he was only trying to celebrate with Eagles fans and that he was pulled back to the field to shake hands with Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer:

"There were a lot of Eagles fans back there, I was excited to celebrate with those Eagles fans and our team and everything like that. It was fun … I'm sure there were some [Cowboys fans] in there but at that point it felt like there was only Eagles fans, we were able to high-five.

"I had to shake everybody's hand out on the field and wanted to be able to celebrate with everybody, and also shake Schotty's hands and their players' hands."

An Eagles representative apparently backed up this account with Pro Football Talk, contending that Sirianni was only celebrating. We'll see if anything else comes of that, but Sirianni is the head coach with less to worry about following that game.

Philadelphia's win went down as the biggest comeback in NFL Thanksgiving history. The Cowboys led 28-10 at halftime and by as many as 21 points late in the third quarter, only for a superb performance by former Cowboys practice-squad QB Joe Milton, now playing for the Eagles, and some brutal mistakes by Dallas to trigger a wild comeback.

Eagles kicker Jake Elliott made a 59-yard field goal for the win, improving the Eagles' record to 4-7 in what has been a trying season for a team that won a Super Bowl less than two years ago.

#2625. What's next for the Twins? Three things Minnesota must do to make a postseason push in 2027 season

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

It has been a surprisingly productive week for the Minnesota Twins. First, catcher Ryan Jeffers accepted the $23.15 million qualifying offer on Tuesday. Jeffers turned down a multi-year offer from the Twins, according to The Athletic, so he's betting on himself. Betting that he'll at least maintain his free agent stock and get paid next offseason.

Then, on Wednesday, the Twins brought back veteran righty Sonny Gray with a two-year contract worth $55 million. There's an opt-out after the first year. Gray, 37, finished fifth in the AL Cy Young voting this season and pitched wonderfully for the Twins in 2022 and 2023. He joins a rotation that, on paper, looks like one of the better starting units in the American League.

Here is Minnesota's rotation depth chart:

"I really don't take it lightly that he chose us," GM Jeremy Zoll told the Associated Press about Gray's return. "He had an abundance of options, and given where he's at in his career, I know how important it is to him. He expressed it quite directly how important it is to win, and this isn't just about having a good season or a winning season. It's about winning and going deep in the playoffs and making a real playoff run."

Matthews could land in the bullpen next season and that might be his long-term home. His stuff should be well suited to a relief role. Gray makes the rotation better and potentially the bullpen better as well by bumping Matthews to relief. Jeffers accepting the qualifying offer keeps a key middle-of-the-order bat in place. A good week for the Twins, this has been.

After a disappointing 77-85 finish this year, Minnesota has already improved significantly in the early days of the offseason. They play in the AL Central. With all due respect, it is not the most imposing division. There's no reason the Twins can't be in the division and wild card races next season. Here now is what's left on Minnesota's offseason to-do list.

Teams had until 5 p.m. ET Friday to offer their pre-arbitration and arbitration-eligible players contracts for 2027. They didn't have to sign them Friday, but they had to tender an offer; otherwise, the player immediately became a free agent. Dozens of players were cut loose at the non-tender deadline, as usual, and two players stood out as non-tender candidates for the Twins: Trevor Larnach and Royce Lewis. Larnach was indeed non-tendered, while Lewis was dealt to the Dodgers.

It's not often a player gets non-tendered after posting a .352 on-base percentage and 120 OPS+, but the writing was on the wall. The Twins had an agreement in place to trade Larnach at the deadline (Astros owner Jim Crane nixed the deal) and they have a very crowded outfield. Also, Larnach had wrist surgery earlier this month. That created some questions going into next season, and the Twins opted to cut him loose.

Larnach had one more year of control remaining and was expected to make over $6 million through arbitration in 2027. I reckon the Twins tried again to trade him prior to Friday's non-tender deadline. In the end, he was non-tendered rather than risk tying $6 million or so up in yet another outfielder, particularly one who is coming off wrist surgery.

Things got so bad this summer that Lewis, who has a .288 on-base percentage in over 1,200 plate appearances the last three years, was sent to Triple-A for a spell, and also moved across the diamond from third base to first base. The Twins could not count on him to provide offense and now he's playing a position with a high offensive bar. That made him expendable.

Lewis, 27, was under team control through 2028 and that extra year was an important consideration for the club. His salary would have been in the $5 million range next season through arbitration, which is pricey but not exorbitant. Now, Lewis will receive a fresh start with the Dodgers, where he can be one of the guys, not the former No. 1 overall pick and expected face of the franchise.

The Twins presumably did not want to give up on a player with as much talent as Lewis. At the same time, they kept trying, and it never worked.

The Twins got a head start on their offseason bullpen shopping when they acquired Jeff Hoffman at the trade deadline. He has one more year remaining on the contract and will be in the team's late-inning mix in 2027.

Here is manager Derek Shelton's bullpen unit at the moment:

Morris is not yet a household name, but he has a great arm and was dominant at times in 2026. The Twins have themselves a nice little late-inning trio in Gómez, Hoffman, and Morris. A spare starter like Matthews or Prielipp could wind up in the bullpen as well. Given the quality of their stuff, they have a chance to make a real impact as relievers.

Clearly though, the middle relief could use some help, and the Twins wouldn't need to spend big dollars to improve it. A second-tier free agent like, say, Andrew Kittredge would be a solid pickup. It's worth giving the Miami Marlins a call to see what it would take to get Anthony Bender and/or Michael Petersen. Point is, the bullpen can be improved, for sure.

The Twins have way more outfielders than outfield spots and that is in no way a bad thing. First and foremost, it allows them to use Byron Buxton as the full-time DH, which could help keep him on the field. Secondly, there's no such thing as too many good players. Depth is important and the Twins certainly have plenty of it in the outfield.

More outfielders than outfield spots is not a problem. It's just something the Twins have to figure out. Even if we assume Buxton will DH and is not part of the outfield mix, here are the outfielders Minnesota must sort through:

Rodriguez is one of the game's 50 or so best prospects and he is out of minor league options, meaning he must go through waivers to go to Triple-A. Obviously, the Twins won't waive him. Non-tendering Larnach allows the Twins to play Rodriguez alongside Jenkins and Keaschall in the outfield, keep Kreidler and Martin on the bench, and keep the others in Triple-A.

#2623. Royce Lewis trade grades: Dodgers land former No. 1 pick; Twins get another arm, arrow-up prospect

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The Los Angeles Dodgers have added a former No. 1 overall pick. The Dodgers are set to acquire infielder Royce Lewis from the Minnesota Twins for right-hander Bobby Miller and minor-league catcher Francisco Espinoza, reports the New York Post. Neither team has announced the trade.

Lewis, 27, was a candidate to be non-tendered prior to Friday's deadline. Rather than cut him loose, the Twins were able to find a trade partner and receive something in return. The No. 1 pick in the 2017 draft has battled injuries throughout his career and posted a .288 on-base percentage the last three years. Lewis simply failed to launch with Minnesota.

The Dodgers figure to use Lewis as a platoon partner for Max Muncy at third base and could also move him around the infield as a utility guy. The Twins moved him from third base to first base this past season. Lewis has played every infield position in the big leagues, though he's had only one inning at shortstop since 2022.

Miller, 27, has been unable to build on his dynamic 2022 rookie season, when he threw 124 ⅓ innings with a 3.76 ERA. He has battled injuries and control issues since then, and the Dodgers moved him into the bullpen this past season. Miller has a 7.75 ERA in 134 ⅔ Triple-A innings the last three years and can be optioned down in 2027.

Espinoza, 19, reached Low Class-A in 2026 and hit .317/.411/.422 with three home runs and strong contact rates in 46 games. He does not rank among the top 30 Dodgers prospects at Baseball America or MLB Pipeline, but Espinoza is an arrow-up prospect and a solid return for a non-tender candidate.

Here now are our grades for the two-for-one trade.

At worst, Lewis will be a high-priced utility guy next season. He's projected to make $5 million or so through arbitration and that simply is not much for the Dodgers, who have a history of getting underperforming hitters to the next level (like Muncy). At best, Lewis could be the new Chris Taylor and reach his offensive ceiling while bouncing between positions.

Espinoza is a good prospect, not a great prospect, and Miller is a reclamation project. Those are easy players for the Dodgers to surrender to take a chance on Lewis and his upside. It may not work. Lewis could continue to get hurt and not hit, but it was a low-cost move and the chance of a reward is significant.

It's a very nice upside play for a team that has hit on a lot of upside plays over the year.

It's a bummer things didn't work out for Lewis and the Twins, but the reality is he was a non-tender candidate, and it wasn't a secret. Minnesota was able to get back a solid prospect in Espinoza and a lottery ticket arm in Miller despite having little leverage. Getting two players for Lewis is a very good outcome under the circumstances.

Giving each team an "A" suggests a win-win, and maybe it will be. There's a chance it's a lose-lose, though. Lewis may not hit, Miller may never rediscover his 2022 form, and Espinoza may not pan out. I see the vision for both teams, though and like it.

The Dodgers rolled the dice on a talented player and the Twins were able to fetch two players for someone they might have otherwise cut loose and sent into free agency.

#2622. Mike Tomlin responds to Steelers ‘dumpster fire’ after Aaron Rodgers debacle

After coaching Aaron Rodgers for one season, Mike Tomlin is watching his downfall from afar.

Rodgers rocked the football world on Wednesday when he went on a scathing rant on "The Pat McAfee Show" about current Steelers coach Mike McCarthy before the quarterback was swiftly cut from the team. Most in Pittsburgh's organization — including owner Art Rooney — are taking McCarthy's side.

Tomlin was not one of those people, opting for neutrality while talking about the situation with Mike Tirico on NBC on Thursday.

"I had a range of emotions watching those course of events yesterday," Tomlin said. "I think the prevailing one is just general sadness. Sad that we might be looking at the end of a legendary career of a quarterback … to see laundry aired out that way in a public forum, those are things that kind of run counterculture to professional football."

Head coach Mike Tomlin (left) walks off the field with Aaron Rodgers after the Steelers' 29-24 win over the Lions on Dec. 21, 2025. Getty Images

Tomlin, now a football analyst for NBC, was Rodgers' head coach in Pittsburgh last season until he resigned in January after 19 years at the helm for the Steelers. McCarthy, who coached Rodgers for 13 years in Green Bay, was hired as his replacement.

Despite Rodgers' allegations of McCarthy falling asleep in team meetings, not watching film and saying "1, 2, 3, Packers" to break down the team after a huddle — the latter of which McCarthy confirmed — Rooney said he has "100 percent confidence" in his head coach and intends to bring him back next season and beyond.

Does Tomlin think his successor will be able to lead the locker room for the final seven games of the season?

"It certainly created some challenges, and challenges is probably an understatement if all of those things are true," Tomlin said. "But his ability to overcome that or inability to overcome that, in my opinion, is based on relationships and the depth of those relationships and how those guys feel about him or how those guys buy in to what he's selling."

Rodgers was popular with the players and coaching staff last season, Tomlin said, making it even more shocking to hear the 42-year-old quarterback sever those relationships on live television.

"He was beloved, and I'm not overexaggerating that," Tomlin said. "He worked at it, and people appreciated his openness getting to know and understand the Steelers culture, to be engaged with teammates.

Aaron Rodgers and head coach Mike Tomlin leave the field after the Steelers' preseason win over the Panthers on Aug. 21, 2025, in Charlotte, N.C. Getty Images

"And particularly from my perspective, I've worked with a lot of veteran players over the years and at times, they lose a little patience for the process, or they lose patience for relationships with younger guys, et cetera. Man, he seemed to embrace all of that and really embrace it in a real, natural way."

The Steelers next turn to Mason Rudolph for Friday's matchup with the Broncos, with the organization squarely in the playoff hunt at 6-4 on the season.

Regardless of how Pittsburgh's season ends up as they move on from their starting QB, the whole debacle is sure to leave a dark scar on the Steelers organization.

"I'm upset about it. It's a dumpster fire," Tomlin said. "And I don't say that in a judgmental way — I've presided over a few dumpster fires in my 19 years. But it certainly is upsetting, and I'm sure Steeler Nation is upset."
